h_vs_bm25_residual: The SYSTEM-H runner, when written, must implement metrics.span_hit exactly as the BM25 runner does — document identity plus character overlap, no section_path term. A SYSTEM-H runner that reused the NATQ-001 overlaps()/dict_overlaps() helpers would silently score a stricter metric and would not be comparable to the frozen 0.375.
h_vs_bm25_control: The SYSTEM-H runner should recompute the BM25 comparator's case_hit@10 from the frozen ranked output and refuse to proceed unless it reproduces 0.375, proving both systems went through one scorer.

boundaries.at_0_65: FAIL is < 0.65, so exactly 0.65 does not fail.
boundaries.the_interval: 0.65 <= case_hit@10 < 0.80 with a significant positive delta is INCONCLUSIVE, stated explicitly in the preregistration.
boundaries.reachability: With 40 validation cases, case_hit@10 moves in steps of 0.025; 0.65 = 26/40 and 0.80 = 32/40 are both exactly attainable, so neither boundary is unreachable.

gap.classification: PROPOSED_PROTOCOL_CORRECTION — NOT APPLIED, REQUIRES COORDINATOR APPROVAL
gap.text: A significant REGRESSION falls through to INCONCLUSIVE. If SYSTEM-H's micro-MRR is worse than BM25 with a 95% interval excluding 0, and case_hit@10 is 0.65 or above, then PASS is false (delta is not > 0) and FAIL is false (the interval does not include 0, and the case_hit floor is met), so the run is labelled INCONCLUSIVE. A system that is decisively worse than the lexical control would not be recorded as a failure.
gap.example: delta = -0.06, 95% interval [-0.10, -0.02], case_hit@10 = 0.70 -> INCONCLUSIVE under the rule as written.
gap.proposal: FAIL: the 95% interval includes 0, OR the 95% interval excludes 0 with a negative mean delta, OR case_hit@10 < 0.65.
gap.consequence: The run remains valid and interpretable; a decisive regression would simply be reported as INCONCLUSIVE with the negative delta visible in the results. This is a labelling weakness, not a source of bias, and it does not by itself block the run.

correction.rendered: Empirically derived from NATQ-002 | True (i.e. not derived)
correction.why: The row label asserts 'empirically derived' and the value asserts 'True', which together state the opposite of the truth. The trailing parenthetical contradicts the row it is attached to rather than repairing it. The defect is that a negated field name (not_empirically_derived_from_NATQ_002) was rendered against a positively-worded label without inverting the value.
correction.reads_as: It is TRUE that the floors were NOT empirically derived from NATQ-002.
correction.corrected_value: No — engineering qualification floors, set before any NATQ-002 score existed

findings: Definition-level: NOT_EQUIVALENT. strict_recall@10 is strictly stricter than case_hit@10 on both axes, so on identical retrieval strict_recall@10 <= case_hit@10 always. The historical 20/40 = 0.50 is therefore a LOWER bound on what case_hit@10 would have been on that dataset, not an estimate of it.

Schema-level: the NATQ-001 predicate is not computable on NATQ-002 as it stands, because NATQ-002 gold evidence carries no section_path. Making the definitions equivalent would require adding a field to frozen gold evidence, which is prohibited and would in any case void the freeze.

Dataset-level: even if the definitions were made identical, NATQ-001 and NATQ-002 are different question sets over the same corpus snapshot with no shared cases. A comparison across them is unpaired and carries no paired statistical interpretation.

The preregistered decision rule does not depend on this. EVAL-NATQ2-H-001 tests SYSTEM-H against the co-run BM25 comparator on the same 40 NATQ-002 cases; the NATQ-001 prior enters only as disclosed context.
